Sleep-pressure / circadian simulation

No measured personal accuracy or energy claim. Changing a schedule is a hypothetical comparison, not evidence of a causal personal benefit.

Original conditional two-process-inspired implementation two-process-v1. UTC hours: waking S'=1-(1-S)*exp(-d/18.2); sleeping S'=S*exp(-d/4.2). Timing constants: Daan, Beersma & Borbely (1984), https://doi.org/10.1152/ajpregu.1984.246.2.R161; two-process background: https://doi.org/10.1111/jsr.12371. No population parameter fit is claimed. B is earliest resolved bedtime; S=0.6 at B-24h. All stated prior sleep is one synthetic block starting at B-24h, then awake to B. Each alternative stays awake from B to its own bedtime, sleeps to its wake, then stays awake through its bedtime+24 elapsed hours. Alternatives are independent. C=cos(2*pi*(t-anchor)/24h); anchor=2026-10-10T22:00:00+00:00, resolved once from 15:00 local on B's local date. A=(1-S+a*(C+1))/(1+2*a), a=0.2. Phase, initial state, prehistory and weight are assumptions, not fitted parameters. Caffeine/light have no modeled effects; phase does not shift. A is a dimensionless illustrative index, higher=more simulated alertness; not probability, KSS, PVT, measured or causal benefit. A sleep-regulation mechanism does not validate a KSS/PVT mapping. No participant data or validation. Equation concepts are literature-derived; implementation is original, with no software code license asserted or borrowed.

Illustrative relative alertness · dimensionless, 0–1. Higher means more alert.
